summary: An opinion piece arguing that local amateur sports teams strengthen community unity, boost local economies, develop youth, promote inclusivity and encourage healthier lifestyles. It uses local examples from the 2023 season and notes that teams run on tight budgets, with only a 2% funding increase. It calls for more funding, business sponsorship, volunteering and general community support.
one_line: An appeal for community members, businesses and the city to support local amateur sports teams for their social, economic, youth and health benefits.
key_facts: On September 14, the Evergreen Falcons played the Maplewood Marauders in a local soccer derby at Evergreen Park.
James "Jimmy" Ellison is a local grocer who also plays goalkeeper for the Evergreen Falcons.
Sarah Johnson spearheaded the October 7th 'Youth Soccer Fest', which caused a spike in sales for local vendors, hotels and eateries.
Mark Sullivan, a high school coach, runs a baseball program that instills discipline, teamwork and a strong work ethic in youth.
Maria Gonzalez, an immigrant mother, found a community in town when her son Luis joined the Riverdale Swimming Club.
On September 21st, during a city council meeting, treasurer Linda Hughes reported that local sports funding rose only 2%, far less than rising costs.
Many local sports teams operate on shoestring budgets, relying on volunteer support and modest membership fees.
Smith Auto Group sponsored the Riverdale Colts, and its profile rose along with the team's success.
Emma Thompson dedicates weekends to organizing Little League tournaments.
The article argues local sports offer physical activity that helps combat issues like obesity and mental health disorders.
The author says investment in local sports is not an expenditure but an investment in community welfare and future prospects.
The piece closes by urging people to fill the stands, lend skills and voice support for increased funding and resources.
